holidays.name: National Chocolate Chip Day
holidays.description: A day to celebrate the glorious little morsels that turn plain cookie dough into a legend. Bake a batch, sneak a few chips straight from the bag, and call it research.
holidays.origin: An unofficial American food holiday that grew out of the love for the chocolate chip cookie, which Ruth Wakefield is credited with inventing at the Toll House Inn in Massachusetts in the 1930s.
holidays.funFact: The chocolate chip cookie is said to have been born when Ruth Wakefield added chopped semi-sweet chocolate to dough, expecting it to melt through. Instead the pieces held their shape, and a classic was created.

holidays.name: National Peanut Butter Cookie Day
holidays.description: A day for the crisscross-fork-marked treat that proves peanut butter belongs in dessert. Pair it with a glass of cold milk for the full experience.
holidays.origin: An unofficial food observance that celebrates a cookie popularized in American kitchens in the early 1900s, after peanut butter became a pantry staple.
holidays.funFact: The famous crisscross fork pattern isn't just for looks. The dough is dense, so pressing it flat helps the cookies bake evenly.

holidays.name: International Day of Families
holidays.description: A United Nations observance that highlights the importance of families, from the ones you were born into to the ones you choose. It is a good excuse for awkward group photos and the dinner table debate over who gets the last dumpling.
holidays.origin: Established by the UN General Assembly in 1993 to raise awareness of issues affecting families around the world.
holidays.funFact: The UN picks a different theme each year, and past themes have ranged from family-friendly policies to the impact of technology on family life.

holidays.name: National Nylon Stocking Day
holidays.description: A day dedicated to the sheer, stretchy, and occasionally snag-prone leg wear that once caused riots in the streets. It is a nod to a very specific moment in fashion history.
holidays.origin: Tied to May 15, 1940, when nylon stockings went on sale nationwide in the United States for the first time, after being introduced to the public at the 1939 World's Fair.
holidays.funFact: On the first day of the national sale in 1940, about 4 million pairs reportedly sold out within hours, and shoppers lined up in huge crowds to get a pair.

holidays.name: Straw Hat Day
holidays.description: A throwback tradition when gentlemen were expected to switch from felt hats to straw boaters, with fashion consequences for anyone who jumped the gun. It is a day to dust off the summer headwear and tip your hat to the season.
holidays.origin: Rooted in early 20th century American and British menswear etiquette, which declared a date in mid-May as the start of straw hat season, with another in September for putting them away.
holidays.funFact: In 1922 in New York City, gangs of young men reportedly knocked off the straw hats of anyone who wore them after the season ended, and the incidents grew into riots now known as the Straw Hat Riot.
